title: Multi-Issue Butterfly Architecture for Sparse Convex Quadratic Programming
problem: General-purpose architectures suffer from poor hardware utilization when performing sparse matrix operations such as factorization and multiplication in convex quadratic programming solvers. Achieving optimal performance is challenged by the sparse nature of objective and constraint matrices.
motivation: Convex quadratic optimization solvers are extensively used across many application domains, making improved performance highly valuable.
method: Multi-Issue Butterfly (MIB) proposes a pipelined spatial architecture with a butterfly computational network where each node has runtime-controlled working modes. For factorization, an elimination tree guides instruction reordering to avoid data hazards from dependencies. For matrix-vector multiplication, data prefetching resolves structural hazards in register file access. Multi-issue execution enables simultaneous instruction issue when hazards are absent to maximize pipeline throughput.
key_novelty: A pipelined spatial butterfly architecture that adapts to sparse matrix structures through sparsity-aware scheduling and specialized hazard avoidance mechanisms.
contributions: Multi-Issue Butterfly spatial architecture with dynamic runtime-controlled working modes for primitive scalar, vector, and matrix operations
Sparsity-aware scheduling method for matrix operations guided by problem structure
Elimination tree-guided instruction reordering for factorization to prevent data hazards
Data prefetching strategy for matrix-vector multiplication to resolve structural hazards

metrics.other: 16.5× less runtime jitter vs CPU, 33.4× less vs GPU

limitations: Limitations and applicability boundaries not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Spatial architecture for accelerating sparse quadratic programming
